coach_checks.text: Entertainment screen time is hard to stop. We would like a realistic stopping point, parking the device, and a gentle transition to an offline activity.
coach_checks.quality_criterion: Three or four relevant choices when supported; include concrete media stopping/parking and transition support.
coach_checks.reply:
A small plan agreed before screen time can make stopping feel more predictable and less abrupt.
1. Before starting, choose a realistic stopping event together, such as the end of an episode or match.
2. Pick a wanted offline activity for afterward; check whether they’d rather eat, rest, connect, or have quiet time.
3. Agree where the device will pause, while keeping it available for communication, learning, accessibility, or safety needs.

goals.title: Agree on a realistic media stopping point
goals.description: Before recreational media starts, agree on one feasible stopping event and the support for ending.
goals.reason: Directly supports agreeing on a feasible endpoint and what help will make stopping manageable, without assuming a universal time limit.

goals.title: Choose an appealing next activity after media
goals.description: Prepare a wanted offline option to bridge the end of recreational media.
goals.reason: Offers a preferred offline bridge after media, while checking that it fits the child’s actual need at that moment.

goals.title: Use a shared device parking agreement
goals.description: Place an entertainment device in an agreed spot for a particular shared or sleep-protecting moment.
goals.reason: Matches the requested device-parking step; agree on a specific pause and preserve access needed for safety or other uses.

drafts.cue: When you are about to start entertainment media.
drafts.why: A clear endpoint can make the ending more understandable; it is a practical family plan, not a validated treatment.
steps: Name one episode ending, save point, or other clear endpoint.
Tell your adult which endpoint you choose.
Say or show your agreed stopping point.
drafts.title: Choose a Media Stopping Point
drafts.kid_hint: You can choose an ending that makes sense for your plan.
drafts.strategy: Offer a few realistic options and agree together before entertainment begins.
drafts.help_text: You can ask for help, take a break, watch, or choose not to practice; essential access stays available.
drafts.completion: You agreed on one stopping point.
drafts.description: Before entertainment media starts, agree on a clear, feasible stopping event, such as an episode ending or game save point.
drafts.instruction: Choose one place or event where you will stop.
drafts.parent_setup: Check that the endpoint fits the activity, family needs, and any accessibility uses; keep essential communication available.

parent_guidance.coach: Ask what ending feels workable and confirm the shared plan before media starts.
parent_guidance.if_hard: Offer a familiar endpoint, a smaller planning step, watching, declining, or a break without penalty.
parent_guidance.observe: Notice whether the agreed endpoint was clear and adjust the plan or adult support afterward.
parent_guidance.prepare: Keep the activity and a few feasible endpoint options in view.

drafts.cue: When you are planning to start entertainment media.
drafts.why: Sharing relevant needs helps the family plan around commitments and access without treating all media use alike.
steps: Think of one save, friend commitment, or access need.
Tell your adult or use your usual communication method.
Agree on how that need fits the stopping plan.
drafts.title: Share What You Need Before Stopping
drafts.kid_hint: Your needs can be part of the plan.
drafts.strategy: Listen for practical needs, then work together on a feasible endpoint and support.
drafts.help_text: You can ask for help, take a break, watch, or choose not to practice; essential access stays available.
drafts.completion: You shared one need that affects your stopping plan.
drafts.description: Before entertainment media starts, tell your adult about a save, friend commitment, or accessibility need that affects ending.
drafts.instruction: Tell your adult one thing you need for a workable ending.
drafts.parent_setup: Make space to discuss saves, online commitments, and accessibility; do not count assistive communication as entertainment.

parent_guidance.coach: Listen without rushing, then help find a realistic endpoint that respects essential access.
parent_guidance.if_hard: Offer choices, a communication aid, watching, declining, or a break without pressure or penalty.
parent_guidance.observe: Notice which practical needs shaped the plan, without judging disclosure or independence.
parent_guidance.prepare: Be available to hear about saves, online commitments, and accessibility needs.

drafts.cue: When you are making a plan before entertainment media.
drafts.why: Agreeing on support in advance can make the plan clearer and avoids relying on surprise or blame.
steps: Choose a reminder or other help that would work for you.
Tell your adult what support you want.
Agree when or how that support will happen.
drafts.title: Agree on Ending Support
drafts.kid_hint: You can help decide what support works for you.
drafts.strategy: Ask what reminder or transition help would be useful, then confirm the plan together.
drafts.help_text: You can ask for help, take a break, watch, or choose not to practice; essential access stays available.
drafts.completion: You agreed on one kind of ending support.
drafts.description: Before entertainment media starts, agree on one useful form of adult support for reaching the stopping point.
drafts.instruction: Choose one kind of help for ending your media.
drafts.parent_setup: Be ready to provide the agreed support and adjust settings or autoplay when needed.

parent_guidance.coach: Confirm the requested support and follow through without changing the agreed endpoint unexpectedly.
parent_guidance.if_hard: Offer one simple support choice, watching, declining, or a break without penalty.
parent_guidance.observe: Notice whether the support was available and revise it if the plan proved unrealistic.
parent_guidance.prepare: Consider available reminders and platform settings before discussing support options.
